subject: Commercial makeup request for increased cold-start cost during warmup delay - Opslytics
messages:
From: Pete Lee <pete@opslytics.io>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Increased infra spend from cold-starts — request for commercial makeup

Hey Sean,

Quick note from our rollout this week — after enabling the Opslytics agent against the Redwood endpoint we saw a 3.6x increase in token spend over the first 72 hours because we hit repeated cold-starts across their user sessions. That was unexpected; our design assumed the warmup optimization you mentioned in the roadmap would be available in Q2.

Numbers attached (opslytics-impact-metrics.csv). This spike is material to our go-live economics and Opslytics is asking if Redwood can provide a temporary commercial makeup (credit or pricing floor) until the "fast-warmup" runtime patch ships.

Can you advise on whether that's something Redwood can support and what the approval path looks like? Julia (cc) is on procurement and asked we escalate quickly so they can keep the pilot going.

Thanks,
Pete Lee
Head of Platform Integrations
Opslytics

---
Attachment: opslytics-impact-metrics.csv (CSV summary, ~12KB)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Pete Lee <pete@opslytics.io>, Julia Brennan <julia@opslytics.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increased infra spend from cold-starts — request for commercial makeup

Pete — appreciate the data and flag. Sorry this hit you during rollout.

Short answer: we can consider a temporary commercial makeup for verified warmup-related spend while we land a fix. I need to confirm scope and an approval cap (finance/legal), and I want Product to confirm the ship estimate so we can time the credit window accurately.

Next steps from my side:
- Loop in Product (lauren_bishop) for ship ETA and how we verify "warmup-related" deltas.
- Share a proposed term for Opslytics to accept (marissa_cole will draft).
- Finance to confirm maximum concession we can approve without exec signoff.

Marissa — assigning you to draft the customer-facing proposal (term + length + measurement).
Lauren — any timeline updates for fast-warmup / warm cache rolling?

Thanks — Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

---
Attachment: none

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Pete Lee <pete@opslytics.io>, Julia Brennan <julia@opslytics.io>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-10T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed temporary makeup terms (draft)

Pete / Julia — attaching a draft term (proposed-makeup-term.docx). Key points in summary:

- Coverage: verified excess token spend attributable to cold-starts during the pre-warmup window (we'll use your agent logs + our request-level traces to reconcile).
- Duration: credit window begins on 2027-05-01 and runs until 14 days after the fast-warmup patch ships (capped at 60 days).
- Cap: we propose a capped credit equal to 40% of the incremental spend above your normal baseline, up to $45,000 total.
- Acceptance: Opslytics to sign the term sheet; credits applied to billing over next invoice cycle.

This is intentionally conservative while we align approvals. If Product can confirm an earlier ship we can shorten the window.

Pete — could you confirm you have the agent traces available for recon?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: proposed-makeup-term.docx (3 pages)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-10T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed temporary makeup terms (draft)

Quick product update / verification plan: 

- Ship ETA: engineering now targets the fast-warmup runtime patch for canary next week (2027-05-17) and full rollout the week after (2027-05-24) barring regressions.
- Verification: we can add a short flag to the runtime that marks requests handled with the warm cache; we’ll retain a short audit log to reconcile with Opslytics traces. That will let us attribute spend precisely to pre/post warmup behavior.
- Risk: if we hit regressions, rollout could slip 1–2 weeks.

Recommendation: approve a timeboxed credit window but cap financial exposure and require joint reconciliation before credits are applied.

Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: none

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-11T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Approval needed — temporary credit for Opslytics (cap request)

Team — I reviewed the draft and the product timeline. Given the strategic nature of this pilot, I'm comfortable supporting a concession but we need executive level signoff for anything > $25k.

Options: 
1) Approve up to $25k today (no further approvals).
2) Approve up to $45k if Revenue VP signs off.

Marissa — please prepare a short one-pager with the proposed financials and customer acceptance so I can take to Revenue leadership. Include the list of metrics we’ll use for reconciliation.

Aditya Rao
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: none

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-11T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Approval needed — temporary credit for Opslytics (cap request)

Update: I spoke with VP Revenue (A. Nguyen) — she approved a one-time credit up to $45,000 provided: 

- The customer signs the term sheet accepting the reconciliation method,
- Credit period capped at 60 days or until fast-warmup is fully rolled out (whichever is sooner),
- Finance gets a final reconciliation package before credits are posted.

Marissa — please route the term to Opslytics and include the acceptance checkbox for the reconciliation plan. Sean — pls confirm customer acceptance and we'll prepare the accounting ticket.

Aditya Rao
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: contract_redline_v2.pdf (redline snippet)
